correctness.rationale: The finite AR(1) Markov-bridge conditional variance equals the Schur complement. The exact trace sum and farthest-endpoint greedy restriction follow algebraically. Under \(n(1-\rho^2)\to0\) a uniform expansion reduces all pairs to a strictly convex continuous quadratic whose global minimizer is (1/5,4/5) with value 1/10. The restricted greedy quadratic has minimum 1/8 and maximum 1/6; dividing proves \(5/4\) and \(5/3\). The 2x2 determinant is strictly maximized by endpoints. Companion exact-rational program checks 1128 finite identities; its finite checks do not prove the asymptotic statement.

The exact 25% unavoidable best-case and 66.7% worst-case asymptotic penalties, together with a determinant-optimal endpoint choice that is trace-suboptimal, answer an intrinsic two-column design question and quantify a practically relevant tie-breaking failure; not a renamed textbook matrix fact.
